_comment: Lightning 2.0 Phase 5: the atomic MUST-MOVE -> LIGHTNING conversion, implementing the specification's twenty-four-step STATE MACHINE - LIGHTNING TRANSITION as one transaction under one Cluster row lock. THE SEAT IS THE ANCHOR: table_seats is never written, and the pool is an overlay in lightning_pool_session pointing at the cash_player_session the seat already had, so stack, baseline, stay clock, rejoin obligation, wallet balance, rake rate, accumulated rake, player identity, cluster membership, VPIP sample and cluster_join_at are unchanged by construction rather than by enforcement - F12 ('no money moves as a result of this transition') is made unreachable rather than merely checked, and the commit still reads the chip total before and after and refuses if it differs, because an invariant nobody measures is an invariant nobody knows about. tables.dealing_halted_at and tables.dealing_halted_reason are the signal the engine reads: finish the hand you are in and start no other. They do not close the table, drop the engine, unseat anybody or touch a stack. They exist because NOTHING IN server/src READ cash_games.cluster_mode before this - zero occurrences in the whole tree - so a converted Cluster's physical tables would have gone on dealing, from the same seats, with the same chips, while the pool believed it owned those players, which is the duplicate-player failure F13, F14 and F15 are written about arriving from an engine that was never told. tables_dealing_halt_is_explained closes the vocabulary to ('lightning_pending_on', 'lightning') and tests dealing_halted_reason IS NOT NULL BEFORE the IN, because x IN (...) with x NULL is NULL rather than false and a CHECK that evaluates to NULL PASSES - without that line the constraint accepts the exact row it was written to reject, and because Phase 10's revert matches on the REASON that table would stay halted for ever. public.cash_cluster_conversion is the durable record the specification requires, carrying all nine mandated fields; its partial unique index on (cluster_id) WHERE status = 'pending' is F13's answer in the database rather than in a worker - two simultaneous converters cannot both open one - and its unique conversion_request_id makes a retry of the SAME request idempotent and answerable with what already happened, which is the difference between 'no-op safely' and 'no-op'. FIVE functions are re-cut here, not three. Three are new and are SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pinned, revoked from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated and granted to service_role only. The other two already existed and are put onto ONE membership predicate - coalesce(tb.is_deleted, false) = false AND coalesce(tb.lifecycle, '') <> 'closed', with NO status filter anywhere - because both decided who belongs to a Cluster using NULLABLE columns. tables.status has a CHECK and is still nullable, because a CHECK that evaluates to NULL PASSES, so status IN (...) and lifecycle <> 'closed' both yielded NULL rather than true and silently dropped a whole board: reproduced on a throwaway backend, a Cluster of 21 converted, 18 entered the pool, and 3 players kept being dealt cash at a board nobody stopped, inside a Cluster that had become Lightning, holding no pool session, with the tick and the balancer stood down so nothing would ever come for them. fn_cash_cluster_live_eligible is the number that AUTHORISES a conversion - uncoalesced it told a Cluster threshold_not_reached however many people were playing on such a board, and wrote a short trigger_population into the audit record - and is re-created by CREATE OR REPLACE, keeping its SECURITY INVOKER, its grants and its 20260921064717 COMMENT. fn_cash_cluster_population is the breakdown beside it; it carried the same predicate in FIVE places and, once live_eligible alone was fixed, reported live_eligible 24 beside seated_eligible 18 on one board - one function contradicting its own headline number - so it is re-cut by ASSERTED SUBSTITUTION, the anchor asserted to occur exactly five times, the result read back from the catalogue. 20260921064717's @live-proof that this predicate occurs five times in that function is knowingly superseded, and a dated Correction is appended to that migration's changelog rather than the proof being quietly reworded. fn_cash_cluster_begin_pending_on is steps 1-6: lock the Cluster in the tick's own lock order, verify MUST_MOVE, ask the verdict, stop below the ON threshold, set PENDING_ON, halt dealing and cancel the Cluster's pending seat moves - it moves NO epoch and creates NO pool session, because the specification creates the Epoch at step 13 after the re-check, which is what makes an abort a two-column clear rather than an unwind. fn_cash_cluster_abort_pending_on is step 11 and acceptance test F04, and is deliberately NOT gated on fn_platform_frozen: leaving a half-converted Cluster must always be possible during an incident, and the break is when incidents are handled. fn_cash_cluster_commit_lightning is steps 9-22: wait for the conversion-safe hand boundary (defined here because the specification names it once and never defines it - no hand_history row of this Cluster with ended_at NULL that started within six hours), RE-ASK the population rather than trusting the decision made at PENDING_ON, refuse and self-abort if any eligible seated player has no open Cluster cash session (checked BEFORE the epoch bump, because after it the self-abort would be refused wrong_state and leave a Cluster in lightning with no pool sessions), bump the Epoch by exactly one with ca.epoch_reason stated, create one Lightning Pool Session per eligible seated player pointing at the cash session they ALREADY had, re-stamp the halt and emit lightning_on. fn_cash_cluster_tick and fn_cash_cluster_balance are also re-created, by the same ASSERTED SUBSTITUTION rather than retyping - the body is read from pg_get_functiondef, the anchor asserted to occur exactly once, one replacement made, every sibling guard asserted to have survived and the result read BACK from the catalogue - because the tick is 40,443 characters and retyping it to add four lines would be the single most dangerous act in the file. They stood down for a reason worth stating: the tick gated on the must_move BOOLEAN, which is the CAPABILITY, and never on cluster_mode, which is the STATE, and a converting Cluster keeps the capability because Phase 10 reverts to must-move seating using these very rules. Law 10.5 - a horse counts exactly like a human - is asserted absent from both bodies after both substitutions. THE CAPABILITY GATE IS SHUT: nothing calls these three functions, deliberately, because a Cluster converted before the Phase 6 matcher exists would strand every eligible player in a pool with no one to deal them a hand.
